galactic.source: Galactic latitude b of a position, in degrees. The first three are real 4FGL-DR4 rows of gll_psc_v35.fit: RAJ2000 and DEJ2000 as the file has them (float32, so given to the digits the file prints) and its own GLAT column to float32's digits. The two poles are defined: the north Galactic pole is at the ICRS position 192.85948, 27.12825 and has b = 90, and the south pole is opposite it. tol is picked: the file's float32 positions put the computed b within 1.6e-5 degrees of GLAT over all 7195 rows of the real file, checked once by hand on 2026-10-30, and 1e-4 is wider than that and far finer than any Fermi ellipse.

cases.name: 4FGL J0004.0+5715, north of the plane in RA, south of it in b
